variables.name: font-size/xs
variables.description:
Intent: Smallest readable text size; used for supplementary information.
Use when: Captions, timestamps, helper text below inputs, legal footnotes, badge labels.
Do not use: For body copy or any text that requires sustained reading — too small for comfort.
Use instead: font-size/sm for secondary body text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/sm
variables.description:
Intent: Secondary text size; slightly smaller than body.
Use when: Supporting copy, table cell content, sidebar labels, secondary descriptions, input helper text.
Do not use: For primary headings or hero content.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/base
variables.description:
Intent: Default body text size — the readable baseline for the system.
Use when: Main body copy, paragraph text, form labels, default UI text.
Do not use: For headings — use font-size/lg and above.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/lg
variables.description:
Intent: Slightly emphasised text; between body and heading.
Use when: Subheadings, lead paragraphs, card titles on smaller cards, section intros.
Do not use: For primary page headings — use font-size/xl or above.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/xl
variables.description:
Intent: Small heading size.
Use when: Panel headers, dialog titles, section headings in sidebars or compact layouts.
Do not use: For body text — will feel too large and reduce density.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/2xl
variables.description:
Intent: Medium heading size.
Use when: Card group headings, page section titles, modal headers.
Do not use: For body or supporting text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/3xl
variables.description:
Intent: Large heading; primary content section titles.
Use when: Page-level h2 headings, feature section titles, prominent labels.
Do not use: Below 600px viewport — scale down to font-size/2xl on mobile.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/4xl
variables.description:
Intent: Major display heading.
Use when: Page h1 titles, onboarding screen headings, large dashboard figures.
Do not use: For anything other than the primary heading on a view.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/5xl
variables.description:
Intent: Hero display text; the largest regular text size.
Use when: Marketing hero headings, splash screens, empty state primary messages.
Do not use: In dense product UI or data-heavy screens — too dominant for functional layouts.
Use instead: font-size/4xl for product UI headings.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/thin
variables.description:
Intent: Hairline weight; purely decorative at large display sizes.
Use when: Giant typographic backdrops, display numerals where the lightness itself is the aesthetic.
Do not use: In product UI at any functional size — illegible below 32px on most screens.
Use instead: font-weight/light for the lightest usable UI weight.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/extralight
variables.description:
Intent: Very light weight; editorial and display use only.
Use when: Large marketing headlines where an airy, refined feel is intentional.
Do not use: In product UI — too light for legible labels or body text.
Use instead: font-weight/light at minimum for UI contexts.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/light
variables.description:
Intent: Below-normal weight for large display text in marketing contexts.
Use when: Hero headings at font-size/4xl or above where the regular weight feels visually heavy — common in Apple-style or editorial layouts.
Do not use: In product UI at any size below 24px — 300 at small sizes is hard to read, especially on non-retina screens. Neither shadcn nor Ant Design uses light weight in product components.
Use instead: font-weight/normal for all product UI text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/normal
variables.description:
Intent: Default reading weight for all body and descriptive text.
Use when: Paragraphs, descriptions, helper text, secondary labels, captions, table cell content. Ant Design uses 400 for all body/description text; shadcn uses it for CardDescription, DialogDescription, p elements.
Do not use: For interactive controls (buttons, tabs, nav links) or headings — those need 500 or 600 to register hierarchy.
Use instead: font-weight/medium for labels and controls.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/medium
variables.description:
Intent: Slightly emphasised weight for interactive controls and UI labels.
Use when: Navigation links, form labels, tab labels, table column headers, secondary buttons, badge text. Ant Design uses 500 for emphasized interactive text; shadcn uses it for Label, nav items, TableHead.
Do not use: For headings — too close to body weight to signal a clear hierarchy jump.
Use instead: font-weight/semibold for titles and headings.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/semibold
variables.description:
Intent: Primary heading weight and strong emphasis for UI titles.
Use when: All component headings — card titles, dialog titles, section titles, sidebar headers, alert titles. Ant Design's fontWeightStrong token is 600; shadcn uses 600 for CardTitle, DialogTitle, AlertTitle, h1–h4.
Do not use: For body copy — creates visual noise when overused at paragraph level.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/bold
variables.description:
Intent: Maximum typographic emphasis; use sparingly.
Use when: Critical callouts, marketing hero text where extra impact is needed beyond semibold, numerical figures in dashboards that need immediate attention (revenue totals, error counts).
Do not use: Routinely in product UI — Ant Design almost never recommends 700; shadcn rarely uses it. Bold loses hierarchy value when overused.
Use instead: font-weight/semibold for all standard headings and emphasis.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/extrabold
variables.description:
Intent: Very heavy weight for extreme emphasis; rarely needed in UI.
Use when: Display numerals on marketing pages, typographic art direction where maximum weight contrast is the design intent.
Do not use: In product UI — heavier than bold without meaningful visual benefit at normal sizes.
Use instead: font-weight/bold for the heaviest practical UI weight.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-weight/black
variables.description:
Intent: Maximum weight; typographic statement only.
Use when: Giant numerals, poster-style marketing layouts, logotype treatments where the weight itself is the visual element.
Do not use: In any functional UI context — illegibly heavy at body sizes, and unnecessarily dominant at heading sizes.
Use instead: font-weight/bold or font-weight/extrabold for strong emphasis.
Status: Stable

variables.name: line-height/none
variables.description:
CSS reference value: 1 (unitless) = leading-none in Tailwind.
For Figma use: do not bind to text styles — use direct px values on each text style instead (single ratio cannot resolve to a correct px value across multiple font sizes).
Use when (CSS/export only): Single-line UI elements — buttons, badges, nav labels.
Do not use: Multi-line text — lines will collide.
Status: Stable

variables.name: line-height/tight
variables.description:
CSS reference value: 1.25 (unitless) = leading-tight in Tailwind.
For Figma use: do not bind to text styles — use direct px values on each text style instead.
Use when (CSS/export only): Display headings, hero titles, large typographic elements.
Do not use: Body copy at small sizes — strains readability.
Status: Stable

variables.name: line-height/snug
variables.description:
CSS reference value: 1.375 (unitless) = leading-snug in Tailwind.
For Figma use: do not bind to text styles — use direct px values on each text style instead.
Use when (CSS/export only): h2–h4 subheadings, card titles, compact multi-line headings.
Do not use: Long-form paragraph text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: line-height/normal
variables.description:
CSS reference value: 1.5 (unitless) = leading-normal in Tailwind.
For Figma use: do not bind to text styles — use direct px values on each text style instead.
Use when (CSS/export only): Paragraphs, descriptions, form helper text, any sustained reading.
Do not use: Headings — will feel too loose.
Status: Stable

variables.name: line-height/relaxed
variables.description:
CSS reference value: 1.625 (unitless) = leading-relaxed in Tailwind.
For Figma use: do not bind to text styles — use direct px values on each text style instead.
Use when (CSS/export only): Long-form articles, documentation, editorial content.
Do not use: Dense product UI — wastes vertical space.
Status: Stable

variables.name: line-height/loose
variables.description:
CSS reference value: 2 (unitless) = leading-loose in Tailwind.
For Figma use: do not bind to text styles — use direct px values on each text style instead.
Use when (CSS/export only): Poetry, pull quotes, highly stylised marketing layouts.
Do not use: Product UI or data-heavy screens.
Status: Stable

variables.name: letter-spacing/tighter
variables.description:
Intent: Tightened tracking for large display text.
Use when: Hero headings and large display type (font-size/4xl and above) where default tracking looks too loose.
Do not use: At small font sizes — negative tracking causes letters to collide.
Use instead: letter-spacing/normal for body and UI text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: letter-spacing/tight
variables.description:
Intent: Slightly reduced tracking for headings.
Use when: font-size/2xl to font-size/3xl headings where a more refined, condensed look is needed.
Do not use: At font-size/base or smaller.
Status: Stable

variables.name: letter-spacing/normal
variables.description:
Intent: Default tracking; the browser and Figma default.
Use when: All body copy, UI labels, buttons, form elements — the safe default for everything.
Do not use: For very large display text — may feel too loose at large sizes.
Use instead: letter-spacing/tight or letter-spacing/tighter for large headings.
Status: Stable

variables.name: letter-spacing/wide
variables.description:
Intent: Increased tracking for emphasis or legibility in specific contexts.
Use when: Uppercase labels, small caps, overline text, metadata tags, ALL CAPS UI elements.
Do not use: For normal mixed-case body text — wide tracking on lowercase copy looks spaced-out and hard to read.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-family/sans
variables.description:
Intent: Primary UI typeface for all interface text.
Use when: Body copy, labels, buttons, inputs, headings — everything that is not code or editorial serif.
Do not use: For code blocks or monospace content.
Use instead: font-family/mono for code; font-family/serif for editorial contexts.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-family/mono
variables.description:
Intent: Monospace typeface for code and technical content.
Use when: Code blocks, inline code snippets, terminal output, token or variable names displayed in UI.
Do not use: For general UI text — monospace has wider character width and will feel visually heavy.
Use instead: font-family/sans for all non-code text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-family/serif
variables.description:
Intent: Serif typeface for editorial or long-form reading contexts.
Use when: Marketing pages, blog posts, article bodies, pull quotes where a traditional editorial tone is intentional.
Do not use: In product UI — serif reads as editorial, not functional.
Use instead: font-family/sans for all product UI text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/8xl
variables.description:
Intent: Oversized display text for maximum visual impact.
Use when: Large hero numbers (pricing, statistics), splash screen numerals, bold marketing headlines where 7xl is not dominant enough.
Do not use: In product UI or anywhere text needs to coexist with other content — this size dominates everything around it.
Use instead: font-size/7xl or font-size/6xl for standard hero headings.
Status: Stable

variables.name: font-size/9xl
variables.description:
Intent: Maximum display size; purely decorative or typographic statement.
Use when: Full-screen typographic art direction, giant background numerals, editorial splash layouts where the number or letter itself is the visual.
Do not use: Anywhere legibility of surrounding content matters — at 128px a single word fills a viewport.
Use instead: font-size/8xl for large but still functional display text.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/none
variables.description:
Intent: Explicitly removes any shadow from an element.
Use when: Resetting shadow on a component that inherits one, flat UI surfaces that must have zero elevation.
Do not use: As the default — omitting a shadow and explicitly setting none are different in CSS cascade terms.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/sm
variables.description:
Intent: Hairline shadow for subtle lift on small elements.
Use when: Buttons, input fields, small cards, tags — elements that need the slightest separation from the background without looking elevated.
Do not use: For floating UI like dropdowns or modals — too subtle to communicate elevation.
Use instead: shadow/default or shadow/md for floating elements.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/default
variables.description:
Intent: Standard shadow for cards and low-elevation surfaces.
Use when: Content cards, list containers, standard panels — elements that sit above the page background but are not floating.
Do not use: For interactive popups or modals — use shadow/md or above for floating UI.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/md
variables.description:
Intent: Medium elevation for floating UI elements.
Use when: Dropdown menus, select popups, date pickers, context menus — elements that float above page content.
Do not use: For inline cards or non-floating surfaces — shadow/default is sufficient there.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/lg
variables.description:
Intent: High elevation for prominent floating containers.
Use when: Popovers, tooltips, command palettes, floating action panels.
Do not use: For modals — use shadow/xl or shadow/2xl for full-screen overlays.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/xl
variables.description:
Intent: Strong elevation for modal-level overlays.
Use when: Dialog modals, sheet panels, drawer overlays — elements that take focus away from the page.
Do not use: For inline elements or cards — disproportionate shadow for non-floating surfaces.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/2xl
variables.description:
Intent: Maximum elevation; deepest shadow in the scale.
Use when: Full-screen modals, onboarding overlays, lightboxes — the topmost layer in a stacking context.
Do not use: For anything below modal level — the opacity and spread are too heavy.
Use instead: shadow/xl for standard dialogs.
Status: Stable

variables.name: shadow/inner
variables.description:
Intent: Inset shadow to signal a recessed or pressed surface.
Use when: Input field backgrounds, pressed button states, search bars — surfaces that should feel sunken rather than raised.
Do not use: On elevated or floating elements — inset shadow conflicts with the elevation metaphor.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/duration/instant
variables.description:
Intent: Zero-duration transition for changes that must feel immediate.
Use when: Checkbox checks, toggle switches, radio selection — binary state changes where animation would feel laggy.
Do not use: For any element that enters or exits the viewport — even instant feels jarring without a tiny transition.
Use instead: motion/duration/fast for the smallest visible transition.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/duration/fast
variables.description:
Intent: Shortest visible transition for small, contained UI feedback.
Use when: Button press feedback, hover state color changes, tooltip appearance on hover, badge updates.
Do not use: For elements larger than ~100px or elements that move across the screen — too fast to track.
Use instead: motion/duration/normal for dropdowns and popovers.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/duration/normal
variables.description:
Intent: Default transition duration for standard UI interactions.
Use when: Dropdown menus appearing, tooltips, select popovers, accordion expand/collapse, tab switching.
Do not use: For large elements that enter from off-screen — feels too abrupt for heavy motion.
Use instead: motion/duration/slow for modals and drawers.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/duration/slow
variables.description:
Intent: Deliberate transition for larger elements entering or leaving the screen.
Use when: Modal dialogs opening, side drawers sliding in, sheet panels, notification toasts entering.
Do not use: For small inline feedback — 300ms on a button hover feels sluggish.
Use instead: motion/duration/normal for small component transitions.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/duration/slower
variables.description:
Intent: Extended transition for page-level changes and intentional emphasis.
Use when: Page-level route transitions, onboarding step animations, hero element reveals, progress completion celebrations.
Do not use: For any repeated or frequent interaction — 500ms becomes frustrating on actions users trigger many times.
Use instead: motion/duration/slow for standard modal and drawer transitions.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/easing/standard
variables.description:
Intent: Default easing for UI state changes that do not involve entering or exiting.
Use when: Color transitions, size changes, opacity shifts on elements already present in the layout — anything that transforms in place.
Do not use: For elements entering from off-screen — use motion/easing/enter. Do not use for elements being dismissed — use motion/easing/exit.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/easing/enter
variables.description:
Intent: Ease-out curve for elements entering the screen. Starts fast, decelerates to rest.
Use when: Modals appearing, dropdowns opening, toasts sliding in, drawers entering — any element that arrives from outside the viewport or appears from nothing.
Do not use: For elements being dismissed or leaving — use motion/easing/exit instead.
Use instead: motion/easing/exit for the reverse (dismissal) animation.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/easing/exit
variables.description:
Intent: Ease-in curve for elements leaving the screen. Starts slow, accelerates out.
Use when: Modals dismissing, dropdowns closing, toasts sliding out, drawers leaving — any element that exits the viewport or disappears.
Do not use: For elements entering — use motion/easing/enter instead.
Use instead: motion/easing/enter for the arrival animation of the same element.
Status: Stable

variables.name: motion/easing/linear
variables.description:
Intent: Constant-speed animation with no acceleration or deceleration.
Use when: Progress bars filling, loading indicators spinning, continuous loops, data-driven animations where the position must map exactly to a value.
Do not use: For UI element transitions — linear motion feels mechanical and unnatural on interactive elements.
Use instead: motion/easing/standard for UI state changes.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/0
variables.description:
Intent: Fully transparent — element is invisible but still occupies space in layout.
Use when: Hiding elements while preserving layout (fade-out start state, visibility toggles).
Do not use: To permanently hide elements — use display:none or visibility:hidden instead.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/10
variables.description:
Intent: Near-invisible tint; barely perceptible presence.
Use when: Very subtle watermark overlays, ghost placeholder backgrounds, extremely faint decorative elements.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/20
variables.description:
Intent: Faint presence; visible but highly transparent.
Use when: Subtle overlay tints, dimmed background decorations, light scrim effects on images.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/40
variables.description:
Intent: Standard disabled state opacity.
Use when: Disabled UI elements — buttons, inputs, selects. Industry standard for signalling non-interactivity without fully hiding the element.
Do not use: For loading states — use opacity/60. Do not use for modal scrims — use opacity/50.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/50
variables.description:
Intent: Half-transparent; balanced between visible and transparent.
Use when: Modal backdrop scrims, image overlays with text on top, split-tone effects.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/60
variables.description:
Intent: Standard loading state opacity.
Use when: Elements in a loading or processing state — buttons with spinners, skeleton content areas awaiting data.
Do not use: For disabled elements — use opacity/40.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/75
variables.description:
Intent: Mostly opaque with slight transparency.
Use when: Frosted-glass effects, translucent panels over content, secondary overlays that show through slightly.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/80
variables.description:
Intent: Ghost element opacity — active but visually receded.
Use when: Ghost buttons in default state, secondary actions that should recede visually, watermark-style elements that remain interactive.
Do not use: For disabled elements — ghost elements are still interactive.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/90
variables.description:
Intent: Near-fully opaque with a barely noticeable transparency.
Use when: Tooltips, popovers, contextual panels where a hint of transparency signals layering without obstructing content.
Status: Stable

variables.name: opacity/100
variables.description:
Intent: Fully opaque — no transparency.
Use when: Default state for all visible elements. Explicitly setting full opacity after a fade-in animation.
Status: Stable
